world.setting: Summer 1900 in a drafty Edwardian London house and an attic study; then the dead city of Charn, the Wood Between the Worlds, and a newborn Narnia
world.register: fantasy with Edwardian realism: dust, gaslight, horse cabs, wet English summer; the wood is lush and warm, Charn is silent and red-lit

digory.name: Digory Kirke
digory.role: protagonist: lonely Edwardian boy, father away in India, carries a secret guilt
digory.look: a slim English boy of about eleven, short untidy brown hair, grey wool jacket and short trousers, scuffed boots, Edwardian 1900 London schoolboy

polly.name: Polly Plummer
polly.role: Digory's neighbour and companion, brave and practical girl
polly.look: a girl of about eleven, dark plaited hair, a long-sleeved cotton dress with a pinafore, buttoned boots, Edwardian 1900 London girl

andrew.name: Uncle Andrew
andrew.role: Digory's uncle, a vain amateur magician who sends children into other worlds
andrew.look: an old man, wild grey hair, a sharply pointed nose, a dressing gown over a waistcoat, pale vain face, Victorian scholar-magician

letty.name: Aunt Letty
letty.role: Digory's aunt, brisk and unimaginative, pushes the children out of the house
letty.look: a stout middle-aged Edwardian woman, hair pinned up, high-necked grey dress with a lace collar, stern face

jadis.name: Jadis, the Witch
jadis.role: last queen of the dead city Charn, cruel and powerful, follows the children into London and then into Narnia
jadis.look: a tall, beautiful woman with black hair and a cold white face, a long dark gown with a silver crown, regal and terrifying

frank.name: Frank the cabby
frank.role: a London cab driver who helps the first sequence with his horse
frank.look: a weathered working-class London cabman, flat cap, heavy wool coat, thick moustache, Edwardian street worker

aslan.name: Aslan
aslan.role: the great lion who sings Narnia into being and sends Digory on his quest
aslan.look: a huge golden-tawny lion with a shining mane, calm and majestic, standing in light

fledge.name: Fledge
fledge.role: the horse Strawberry, transformed into a winged horse by Aslan, carries Digory
fledge.look: a strong chestnut horse with large feathered wings folded at its shoulders, Narnian and magical

mrs-kirke.name: Mrs Kirke
mrs-kirke.role: Digory's mother, slowly dying upstairs in bed; her illness drives Digory's choice
mrs-kirke.look: a pale thin Edwardian woman in a white nightgown and shawl, lying in a bed, frail and weary

helen.name: Helen
helen.role: Frank the cabby's wife; Aslan crowns the couple as the first king and queen of Narnia
helen.look: a plump, kindly London woman of about fifty, hair in a bun, a dark wool dress and shawl, Edwardian working-class wife

attic.look: dusty London attic study, a highback chair, a ticking clock, a red wooden tray holding yellow and green rings

london-street.look: a cold, wet Edwardian London street with gaslamps and horse cabs

wood-between-worlds.look: a warm, lush wood of still pools, each one leading to a different world

charn.look: the dead city of Charn: red-lit, silent, ruined towers and a great bell

narnia-garden.look: a newborn Narnia: a bright cold forest under a new sky, a young apple tree, stars

objects.why: the yellow and green rings: the book's central mechanism, sending people between worlds; no icon yet, Phase 4 should draw it
the lamp-post standing in the snowy wood, the way back to London
the apple Digory brings back, a magic fruit that protects Narnia from Jadis
the bell in Charn: striking it wakes Jadis and the dead city's power
the young tree planted in Narnia, grown from the apple
Charn as a dead city, and the death Digory fears for his mother
the rings pull everyone back home; Digory's home is the sickroom
the wardrobe door foreshadowed by the rings' doorway

spine.claim: Digory is a powerless boy in a grieving house, and Uncle Andrew's rings offer him a secret power.
The rings send the children into other worlds, and Jadis follows them back into London.
In Charn, striking the bell wakes Jadis, and Digory's curiosity becomes the first disaster.
Digory must choose between saving his mother with the apple and the danger he has released.
Digory refuses to steal, and his refusal grows the tree that shelters Narnia.
